HISTORY owns Euripides's Medea as an actual 431 BCE play; theology owns the Medea-Jason cycle it dramatizes.

name: Bellerophon, Pegasus, and the lead-tipped spear
scope: The Corinthian hero who rode Pegasus, killed the Chimera, and tried to fly too high. T1: BELLEROPHON is a young prince of CORINTH, sometimes called son of Poseidon, sometimes of King Glaucus. He is sent as a young man to King PROETUS of Tiryns after an accidental killing; Proetus's wife STHENEBOEA (in some sources Anteia) tries to seduce him, and when he refuses, she accuses him falsely to her husband. Proetus, unwilling to break the guest-friendship-code by killing him personally, sends him to his father-in-law KING IOBATES of Lycia with a SEALED LETTER instructing that the BEARER BE KILLED (Homer, Iliad 6.155-197 -- 'the letter of Bellerophon' is Greek myth's earliest reference to writing). T2: Iobates opens the letter after entertaining Bellerophon for nine days; unwilling to break the guest-friendship, he too sends Bellerophon on an ERRAND meant to be fatal -- to kill the CHIMERA, a monster ravaging Lycia (Homer, Iliad 6.179-182). The Chimera is Typhon's daughter (like Cerberus and the Hydra); her front is a LION, her middle a GOAT (a goat-head springs from her back), and her rear is a SERPENT, and she BREATHES FIRE from all mouths. T3: no man on foot can approach a fire-breathing beast. On advice of the seer POLYIDUS, Bellerophon spends the night in ATHENA's temple; the goddess appears in a dream and lays beside him a GOLDEN BRIDLE. When he wakes the bridle is really there. Taking it to the SPRING OF PIRENE at Corinth (where PEGASUS -- the winged horse born from Medusa's neck when Perseus struck -- comes to drink), Bellerophon slips the golden bridle over Pegasus's head and tames the winged horse for himself (Pindar, Olympian 13.63-92). T4: he flies against the CHIMERA. The trick is that arrows glance off her burning hide and no spear can pierce it. Bellerophon fits his spear with a LUMP OF LEAD at its tip; he flies in, thrusts the lead-tipped spear DOWN INTO HER MOUTH; the Chimera's OWN FIRE MELTS THE LEAD; the molten lead runs down her throat and SUFFOCATES her (Apollodorus 2.3.2, the standard version -- the lead-in-the-mouth detail is the most famous). Bellerophon returns triumphant. T5: emboldened by his victories (he next defeats the Solymi and the Amazons, other tasks Iobates sets), Bellerophon commits HUBRIS -- he attempts to fly Pegasus UP TO OLYMPUS itself, to sit among the gods. ZEUS is offended and sends a GADFLY to sting Pegasus in mid-flight; the horse throws him. Bellerophon FALLS ALL THE WAY BACK TO EARTH. In Homer's stark line (Iliad 6.200-202) he lives on afterward 'hated by all the gods, wandering the Aleian Plain alone, eating out his heart'; Pegasus flies on to Olympus, where Zeus keeps him as the carrier of his THUNDERBOLTS (later placed as the constellation PEGASUS). Further rungs: Bellerophon's 'letter' in Iliad 6 is the only reference to writing in Homer, calling it 'baneful signs, deadly to look on'; Pegasus's earlier scene at Perseus's beheading of Medusa is the connective tissue between the two hero-strands; the Chimera-in-Lycia is one of many Greek monsters said to originate in the volcanic 'Chimaera' natural-gas vents still burning today in Lycia (modern Turkey near Cirali), still called 'Yanartas' the burning stones.
source: PRIMARY: Homer, Iliad 6.152-211 (Glaucus tells Diomedes the Bellerophon story -- the false accusation by Stheneboea, the sealed letter, Iobates's tasks, the Chimera, the later fall from Pegasus 'hated by all the gods'); Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 2.3.1-2 (the sealed letter, Athena's bridle at Pirene, the lead-tipped spear, killing Chimera by melting lead down its throat, the Olympus flight and fall); Pindar, Olympian 13.63-92 (Athena's dream, the golden bridle, taming Pegasus at Pirene); Hesiod, Theogony 319-325 (the Chimera as offspring of Typhon and Echidna, lion-goat-serpent). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Bellerophon' (403; via browser 2026-09-04) and Wikipedia 'Bellerophon', 'Pegasus', 'Chimera (mythology)' -- Proetus and the sealed letter (earliest writing reference in Greek myth), Iobates's tasks, the Chimera as lion/goat/serpent breathing fire, Athena's golden bridle in a dream, taming Pegasus at the Pirene spring, the lead-tipped spear that melts in the Chimera's own flame, the flight to Olympus and Zeus's gadfly, Pegasus continuing on to become Zeus's thunder-carrier.
framing_note: The 'melt the lead in the monster's own mouth' + 'fell from Pegasus' ladder. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (Bellerophon TIPPED HIS SPEAR WITH LEAD, and the Chimera's OWN FIRE melted the lead down her throat and suffocated her from inside) and T5 (Bellerophon tried to fly Pegasus up to OLYMPUS and Zeus sent a GADFLY that stung the horse mid-flight and threw him). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem name Pegasus AND ask what he rode -- describe the SCENE (a young man at Athena's temple, a golden bridle beside him at dawn, a winged horse at a spring) and let the recall be the HORSE (Pegasus), the BRIDLE (golden, from Athena), or the KILLING-TRICK (lead-tipped spear that melts inside the beast). SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way one would tell of Icarus's wax wings melting near the sun, or of the tower of Babel toppled by Yahweh, or of Loki's punishment for trying to escape the gods -- the mortal who tried to rise above his station and was cast down. DISTRACTOR MINE: other Pegasus riders (only Bellerophon in Greek myth -- but wrong choices might name Perseus, whose flying is by winged sandals from Hermes, not Pegasus), other 'letter of death' stories (Uriah the Hittite in the Old Testament from a different pillar -- adjacent-real, must be distinguished), other multi-part monsters (the Nemean Lion, Cerberus, Ladon -- adjacent, all Typhon-offspring). Wrong ways to kill the Chimera: not arrows (bounced), not fire (she IS fire), not a normal spear; specifically LEAD melted by her own flame.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Lycia in southwest Turkey with the real natural gas-vents at Yanartas (proposed origin of the Chimera myth); Corinth as a real Greek city with the Pirene spring; theology owns the flying-horse story. LITERATURE: 'the letter of Bellerophon' is Homer's only reference to writing -- a bridge to the language-and-alphabet strand of history.

name: Meleager, Atalanta, and the Calydonian Boar
scope: The great hunt in Calydon, first blood by a woman, and the firebrand on the hearth. T1: MELEAGER is a prince of CALYDON in Aetolia, son of King OENEUS and Queen ALTHAEA. When he was seven days old, the three MOIRAI (the Fates) appeared at his mother's fire and prophesied his life-length: MELEAGER WOULD LIVE ONLY AS LONG AS A CERTAIN FIREBRAND on the hearth was unburnt. Althaea sprang up, snatched the burning log from the fire, doused it, and hid it in a chest for safekeeping (Ovid, Metamorphoses 8.451-458). T2: years later, King Oeneus offers first-fruits sacrifices to all the gods but forgets ARTEMIS. Artemis in fury sends a MONSTROUS BOAR to ravage Calydon -- larger than any ordinary boar, tusks like elephant-tusks, uprooting orchards and killing farmers. Meleager summons the CALYDONIAN BOAR HUNT and invites the greatest heroes of Greece: THESEUS, JASON, CASTOR and POLLUX, PELEUS (Achilles's father-to-be), TELAMON (Ajax's father-to-be), Meleager's uncles TOXEUS and PLEXIPPUS on his mother's side, and -- controversially -- the huntress ATALANTA. T3: the hunt begins. Meleager is in love with Atalanta. Several hunters are killed or injured (one hunter's own spear-throw kills his companion; the boar gores others). ATALANTA, armed with a bow, is the FIRST TO STRIKE THE BOAR -- her arrow draws first blood, wounding him behind the ear. As the boar charges, Meleager delivers the KILLING SPEAR-THRUST. T4: Meleager, as leader of the hunt, has the RIGHT TO AWARD THE HIDE and TUSKS as trophy. He gives them to ATALANTA because she drew first blood. His uncles TOXEUS and PLEXIPPUS are enraged -- a WOMAN getting the prize of the greatest hunt in Greek memory -- and try to take the hide from her by force. Meleager, defending her, KILLS both his uncles (Ovid 8.435-444). T5: when Althaea learns her SON has killed her BROTHERS, she is torn between mother-love and blood-vengeance for her family. She goes to the hidden chest, takes out the FIREBRAND that has been safe for so many years, and THROWS IT ONTO THE FIRE. Far away in Calydon, Meleager -- who was in perfect health -- suddenly feels a burning inside him. As the firebrand blackens and crumbles in his mother's hearth, Meleager BURNS AWAY FROM WITHIN and dies. Althaea, realizing what she has done, kills herself. Meleager's sisters weep so long and hard that Artemis turns them into GUINEAFOWL (called 'meleagrides' in Greek -- the guineafowl's Latin scientific genus is still 'Meleagris' today, from the sisters). Further rungs: some sources have Meleager and Atalanta as lovers; Ovid's account is the fullest; Homer, Iliad 9.529-599 tells a different older version in which Meleager withdraws from battle after a quarrel with his mother rather than dies from a firebrand -- and this Homeric version is used in the Iliad as a warning-story TO ACHILLES; the tusks of the Calydonian Boar were said to have been kept at the temple of Athena at Tegea in Arcadia for centuries and later carried off by the emperor Augustus to Rome (Pausanias 8.46.1-4).
source: PRIMARY: Ovid, Metamorphoses 8.260-546 (the whole hunt, the firebrand prophecy, the boar, Atalanta first blood, the uncles killed, Althaea burning the log, Meleager burning from within, the sisters turned into guineafowl); Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 1.8.2-3 (parallel prose account); Homer, Iliad 9.529-599 (the older Homeric version with Meleager withdrawing from battle -- variant); Pausanias 8.46.1-4 (the tusks preserved at Tegea, taken by Augustus); Hesiod, Ehoiai fragments. CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Meleager' and 'Calydonian Boar' (403; via browser 2026-09-04) and Wikipedia 'Meleager', 'Calydonian Boar', 'Althaea' -- the firebrand prophecy at his birth, Artemis sending the boar because Oeneus omitted her from sacrifice, the great hunt including Atalanta, Atalanta drawing first blood with her arrow, Meleager killing the boar, awarding the hide to Atalanta, the uncles Toxeus and Plexippus killed for trying to take it back, Althaea throwing the firebrand back in the fire, Meleager burning from within, the sisters becoming guineafowl (meleagrides). CORROBORATE AT BUILD: whether Ovid names the uncles Toxeus and Plexippus (yes -- Metamorphoses 8.440-444).
framing_note: The 'life tied to a log' ladder -- the mother-burns-her-own-son twist is the dinner-test moment. Dinner-test payoff: T5 (his mother went to the chest, took out the FIREBRAND from his birth, and threw it back on the fire -- and he BURNED from inside as it crumbled) and T4 (Atalanta drew FIRST BLOOD, so Meleager gave her the hide, and his uncles tried to take it back and he KILLED THEM). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem name the firebrand AND ask what killed Meleager -- describe the SCENE (the Fates at a cradle, a mother snatching a log from the fire, years later a chest opening) and let the recall be the OBJECT (firebrand), the ACT (his mother threw it back on the fire), or the trigger (he killed her brothers over Atalanta's prize). SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way one would tell of Baldr's mother Frigg making every thing swear not to harm him except the mistletoe, or of Diarmuid and the boar of Ben Bulben (which is a different Celtic boar-story -- distractor mine) -- the hero-life tied to a specific vulnerability. Kids can handle it. DISTRACTOR MINE: other giant boars (the Erymanthian Boar killed by Heracles -- adjacent-real from this same strand, must be distinguished; the Crommyonian Sow killed by Theseus; the boar of Ben Bulben that kills Diarmuid -- Irish pillar, must be distinguished), other Fates-prophecy-at-birth stories (Achilles dipped in the Styx by Thetis; Baldr's mother's oaths from every thing), other 'mother turns against son' scenes. Wrong hunter drawing first blood: not Jason, not Theseus; ATALANTA.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Calydon in Aetolia (western Greece) as a real Bronze-Age town; theology owns the boar hunt. ANIMAL bank owns real guineafowl -- their genus name 'Meleagris' comes from this myth (the sisters turned into guineafowl -- meleagrides); theology owns the naming-story.

name: Atalanta: the she-bear, the boar, and the golden apples
scope: The great huntress: exposed as an infant, saved by a bear, first blood at Calydon, beaten in a footrace by golden apples. T1: ATALANTA is the only child of King IASUS of Arcadia (in some sources King Schoeneus of Boeotia). Wanting a son, he had her EXPOSED as an infant on MOUNT PARTHENION to die. A SHE-BEAR SACRED TO ARTEMIS -- whose own cubs had been killed by hunters -- found the baby and NURSED HER at the same teats where her cubs had suckled. Hunters later found Atalanta living wild among the bear-cubs and raised her (Apollodorus 3.9.2; Aelian, De Natura Animalium 13.1). T2: she grew up as a huntress dedicated to Artemis, sworn to VIRGINITY. Two CENTAURS (Rhoecus and Hylaeus) attempted to violate her in the forest; she shot them both dead. She was the ONLY WOMAN admitted to the CALYDONIAN BOAR HUNT (see the Meleager rung) where she drew FIRST BLOOD on the monstrous boar, and Meleager awarded her the hide -- which triggered the whole tragedy of Meleager's death. T3: her father recognized her as an adult and welcomed her back; but he wanted her married. She agreed on one condition -- any suitor must OUTRUN HER in a footrace, and she was the fastest runner in Greece. LOSERS would be EXECUTED. Many young men tried and were killed. T4: a young man named MELANION (in Boeotian sources, HIPPOMENES) prayed to APHRODITE for help. The goddess gave him THREE GOLDEN APPLES from the garden of the Hesperides (or in some tellings from her own sacred grove at Tamasus in Cyprus). Melanion took them into the race. Every time Atalanta drew alongside him, he threw one of the apples off to the side of the track. Each time, Atalanta STOPPED to pick up the beautiful glowing apple -- Aphrodite made them irresistible. On the third apple she was too far behind to catch up, and Melanion crossed the finish first (Ovid, Metamorphoses 10.560-680). T5: Atalanta married Melanion as promised. But Melanion forgot to thank Aphrodite. In her anger, the goddess struck them with sudden desire in a SACRED PRECINCT (in Ovid a temple of Cybele, in others a temple of Zeus) -- they lay together in the holy place, an outrage against the god. As punishment they were TRANSFORMED INTO LIONS and yoked to the chariot of CYBELE, the Mother of the Gods, forever after (Ovid 10.681-707). Further rungs: some sources have Atalanta among the Argonauts; her son by Meleager (in versions where they were lovers) is named PARTHENOPAEUS -- one of the Seven Against Thebes; the story explains via folk-etymology why lions in Greek myth are said not to breed with lions but with leopards -- because Atalanta and Melanion were once human and cannot mate as beasts (Ovid 10.702-705 explains the lion-not-with-lion belief this way).
source: PRIMARY: Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 3.9.2 (birth, exposure, she-bear, hunters raising her, the two centaurs, the Calydonian Boar Hunt, the golden apples race, transformation into lions); Ovid, Metamorphoses 10.560-707 (the fullest version -- the footrace with three golden apples from Aphrodite, the sacred precinct, the lion punishment); Aelian, De Natura Animalium 13.1 (the bear nursing Atalanta); Hesiod, Ehoiai fragments 72-76 (the race and the apples); Xenophon, Cynegetica 1.7. CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Atalanta' (403; via browser 2026-09-04) and Wikipedia 'Atalanta', 'Melanion', 'Hippomenes' -- father wanting a son, exposed on Mount Parthenion, suckled by a she-bear sacred to Artemis, raised by hunters, virgin huntress, centaurs killed, Calydonian Boar first-blood, footrace with the losers executed, Melanion/Hippomenes given three golden apples by Aphrodite (from the Hesperides or from Cyprus), Atalanta stopping to pick them up, marriage, sacred precinct violated, transformation into lions of Cybele's chariot. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: whether the winning suitor is standardly Melanion (older) or Hippomenes (Ovid) -- both names are used depending on tradition.
framing_note: The 'raised by a bear, beaten by apples' ladder -- Atalanta gets a full rung of her own (in addition to her appearance in Meleager's). Dinner-test payoff: T4 (a young man beat her in the footrace by DROPPING THREE GOLDEN APPLES from Aphrodite off the track, and she STOPPED to pick each one up) and T1 (her father exposed her to die and a SHE-BEAR NURSED HER at the same teats where hunters had killed her cubs). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let the stem name the apples AND ask what stopped her in the race -- describe the SCENE (a princess who cannot be caught, suitors executed for losing, one desperate young man praying to Aphrodite) and let the recall be the OBJECTS (three golden apples), the SOURCE (Aphrodite, from the Hesperides or Cyprus), or the WINNER (Melanion or Hippomenes). SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way one would tell of Scathach training Cuchulainn, or of the Valkyries choosing the slain -- a warrior-woman story on the same plane as the boy-hero stories. DISTRACTOR MINE: other golden apples (the Judgment of Paris apple thrown by Eris -- adjacent-real, must be distinguished; the apples of the Hesperides fetched by Heracles -- also from this strand, in fact these apples may be from that same tree), other suckled-by-beasts (Romulus and Remus by the she-wolf -- Roman pillar; Cyrus by a she-dog in Herodotus), other virgin-huntress figures (Artemis herself; Camilla in Virgil). Wrong beasts of Cybele's chariot: not deer (Artemis's), not doves (Aphrodite's), not eagles (Zeus's); LIONS -- and specifically Atalanta and Melanion in lion-form.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Mount Parthenion in Arcadia as a real mountain; theology owns the bear-nurse and race stories. ANIMAL bank owns real bears nursing cubs; theology owns the bear-sacred-to-Artemis nursing a human infant.
